problem: Plain (lo, hi) pairs are now read as half-open [lo, hi) instead of closed [lo, hi], so every public function silently returns different sets (single points like (1,1) are dropped, shared endpoints vanish from union/intersection/difference), (lo, None) is now accepted where main raised ValueError, and error messages show a 4-tuple the caller never passed.

The main module now imports reference_impl, found through sys.path rather than next to the file, so it fails with ModuleNotFoundError when run from elsewhere and can load an unrelated reference_impl.py (seen loading /tmp/reference_impl.py).

parse calls another class's method (_ref._Algebra.parse) with this class's self, which pyright rejects, would fail on Python 2, and relies on validate_bounds/is_number staying identical in two copies.
The repository has no tests at all, so the change in results for every public function went uncaught.
The parse docstring stating its return value and when it raises ValueError was removed, and nothing records the new default for plain pairs.
